questions.q: Where do you turn on "Allow multiple values" for a parameter?
options: The General tab of the Report Parameter Properties dialog
The Tablix Properties dialog
It's a report-server-only setting, not available at design time
The Default Values tab only
questions.explain: Allow multiple values is a checkbox on the General tab of Report Parameter Properties.

questions.q: If a dataset query used WHERE StoreID = (@StoreID) for a single-value parameter, what must it become once that parameter allows multiple values?
options: WHERE StoreID != (@StoreID)
WHERE StoreID IN (@StoreID)
WHERE StoreID LIKE (@StoreID)
It can stay exactly the same
questions.explain: The IN operator tests for inclusion in a set of values — the equals operator can't compare a column against an array of selected values.

questions.q: What must change on a Tablix filter that references a parameter after it becomes multi-value?
options: The filter's Expression must reference a different field
Nothing — Tablix filters are unaffected by multi-value parameters
The filter must be deleted entirely
The filter's Operator must switch from equals to In
questions.explain: Just like the dataset query, any Tablix filter referencing the parameter needs its Operator changed from equals to In to correctly test against a set of values.

questions.q: What does a multi-value parameter's dropdown add automatically, once it has an available values list?
options: A search box only, with no checkboxes
A numeric ranking of each value by frequency
Nothing changes visually — it looks identical to a single-value dropdown
A checkbox for each item plus an automatic (Select All) option at the top
questions.explain: Once multi-value is on, each item in the dropdown gets a checkbox, and an automatic (Select All) item appears at the top to check or clear every value at once.

questions.q: Why can't an expression like [@StoreID] alone still display cleanly in a page footer once the parameter is multi-value?
options: Because page footers cannot contain any parameter expressions
Because the parameter's value is now an array, not a single value, and needs Join() to flatten it into readable text
Because multi-value parameters can no longer appear in text boxes
Because [@StoreID] syntax is removed entirely once multi-value is enabled
questions.explain: Parameters!StoreID.Value now returns an array of selected values, so a direct reference needs something like Join(Parameters!StoreID.Label, ", ") to turn it into one readable string.
